claims.text: ACT (eg, PO artemether/lumefantrine) is the most rapidly active tx and, in many situations, the tx of choice.
claims.quote: Artemisinin-based combination therapy, such as oral artemether/lumefantrine, is the most rapidly active treatment and, in many situations, it is the treatment of choice.
claims.locator: Treatment of Malaria › Efficacy and adverse effects of drugs available

claims.text: Uncomplicated P. falciparum: PO options include artemether/lumefantrine and atovaquone/proguanil.
claims.quote: For uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, oral options include artemether/lumefantrine and atovaquone/proguanil.
claims.locator: Treatment of Malaria › P. falciparum malaria

claims.text: Take both w food or a fatty drink such as milk to enhance absorption.
claims.quote: Patients should take both artemether/lumefantrine and atovaquone/proguanil with food or a fatty drink such as milk to enhance absorption.
claims.locator: Treatment of Malaria › P. falciparum malaria

claims.text: Both: not recommended in pregnancy, esp the first trimester (insufficient safety data), but may be used if other options are unavailable or poorly tolerated and benefits outweigh risks.
claims.quote: These medications are not recommended for use during pregnancy, especially in the first trimester because of insufficient safety data, but may be prescribed if other options are unavailable or poorly tolerated and if the benefits outweigh the risks.
claims.locator: Treatment of Malaria › P. falciparum malaria

claims.text: Alt: mefloquine; can be given to adults and children of all ages, including in pregnancy.
claims.quote: Alternatively, mefloquine may be given; it can be prescribed to adults and children of all ages, including during pregnancy.
claims.locator: Treatment of Malaria › P. falciparum malaria

claims.text: Mefloquine CI: hx of psychiatric disorders, seizures or cardiac conduction abnormalities.
claims.quote: Mefloquine is contraindicated in patients with a history of psychiatric disorders, seizures, or cardiac conduction abnormalities.
claims.locator: Treatment of Malaria › P. falciparum malaria

claims.text: Less commonly: chloroquine, quinine or mefloquine.
claims.quote: Treatment regimens for acute disease include artemisinin-based combination therapy, the most rapidly acting regimen, the fixed combination of atovaquone and proguanil, and, less commonly, chloroquine, quinine, or mefloquine.

claims.text: Chloroquine: an option for P. falciparum only in Haiti, Dominican Republic, Central America west and north of the Panama Canal and parts of the Middle East; resistance is widespread elsewhere.
claims.quote: Chloroquine is an option for P. falciparum malaria in Haiti, Dominican Republic, Central America west and north of the Panama Canal, and parts of the Middle East. However, resistance to chloroquine is now widespread among P. falciparum elsewhere in the world.
claims.locator: Treatment of Malaria › P. falciparum malaria

claims.text: Severe malaria: IV artesunate, the only drug available in the US for parenteral tx.
claims.quote: It requires urgent treatment, preferably with IV artesunate, which is the only drug available in the United States for parenteral treatment of severe malaria (or for patients who cannot take drugs orally).

claims.text: After IV artesunate: monitor Hgb for 4 weeks (delayed hemolysis).
claims.quote: Due to the risk of delayed hemolysis, which is a frequent complication in hyperparasitemic malaria treated with IV artesunate (5), hemoglobin levels should be monitored for 4 weeks after therapy.
